items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Chittison had taken a trio in after we left and had a very nice guitar/with him who's name was Everett Barkedale.

ctx.x: After quite a few months at the Angel, we began to feel that we were liked well enough and popular enough to ask for a raise in salary and we did ask for it. We got exactly the same answer from Jacoby that Barney Josephson had given us when we asked him for a raise. Jacoby said: You boys deserve a raise and we thought the matter was settled. We did not speak about the amount because we thought that it would be at least five dollars each.

One night shortly after we had asked for the raise. Herman Chittison came to the club and when we received our pay envelope at the end of the week, there was a two-weeks notice which stated that our service would not be required after two more weeks. Chittison had taken a trio in after we left and had a very nice guitar/with him who's name was Everett Barkedale.

We started getting some jobs from the Joe Glaser booking agency and once we had an afternoon party to play for a very wealthy family by the name of Managers who owned the hotel Astor. The party was in honour of a son who was a medical ensign in the Navy and all the young men who were invited were in the Navy also.
